### Summary

REST cookie parsing turns `authenticationToken=j:%7B%7D` into `{}`. REST authentication passes that object to the XO token provider without requiring a string. The token collection treats `{}` as an unfiltered lookup and returns its first token; the provider authenticates as that token's owner if it is unexpired. The authenticated `/rest/v0/users/me/authentication_tokens` route then returns reusable login token IDs.

### Details

1. In `packages/xo-server/src/api/session.mjs`, function  `signIn(credentials)` has **no `params` schema** (unlike the deprecated `signInWithToken`, which declares `token: { type: 'string' }`), so `credentials.token` can be any JSON value.
2. `packages/xo-server/src/xo-mixins/authentication.mjs`, token provider:
   ```js
   this.registerAuthenticationProvider(async ({ token: tokenId }, { ip } = {}) => {
     if (!tokenId) return          // {} is truthy → passes
     const token = await app.getAuthenticationToken(tokenId)
     ...
     return { bypassOtp: true, expiration: token.expiration, userId: token.user_id }
   ```
3. `getAuthenticationToken(properties)` explicitly accepts an object, and `_getAuthenticationToken(id, properties)` does `this._tokens.first(properties ?? id)`.
4. `Collection#first(properties)` -> `_get(properties)`; in `collection/redis.mjs`, `if (isEmpty(properties)) return redis.sMembers(prefix + '_ids')…` → **all tokens**. Non-empty objects on indexed fields (`user_id`, `client_id`) do an index lookup → token of the chosen user.
5. HTTP paths: `index.mjs` (`req.cookies.token` → `isValidAuthenticationToken`), `xo-mixins/rest-api.mjs` and `@xen-orchestra/rest-api` middleware (`cookies.authenticationToken ?? cookies.token` → `authenticateUser({ token })`). `cookie-parser` turns `j:`-prefixed cookie values into parsed JSON, so `authenticationToken=j:{}` yields `{}`.

### Proof of concept

The object cookie returned 200 with unexpired token IDs, and one ID worked on a fresh request as an admin account. The attacker does not choose which token the empty-object lookup returns. Authentication succeeds only if the token returned first is unexpired and belongs to an existing user; if it is expired or its user was deleted, the request fails without trying another token.

```bash
curl -b 'authenticationToken=j:{}' https://<ip>/rest/v0/users
```

### Impact

An adversary can bypass authentication and perform actions with 'Admin' privilege. Xen Orchestra compromise can lead to arbitrary code execution on managed pools and a full XCP-ng node takeover as root.

Package bundles a collection of skill directories containing various helper scripts. Static pattern matches fired on routine network primitives: a Python scraper (bundled-skills/junta-leiloeiros/scripts/base_scraper.py) and an API server script (serve_api.py) that reference `ping`/GET/POST, a benchmark harness (bundled-skills/loki-mode/benchmarks/run-benchmarks.sh), an rclone install helper (bundled-skills/rclone-cli/scripts/install.sh) that runs `curl https://rclone.org` to fetch the rclone installer from its official project domain, and a youtube-notetaker verification script using `curl` against GET endpoints. Matches reflect keyword co-occurrence (curl/ping/GET/POST) in utility scripts rather than exfiltration shapes: no hardcoded attacker C2, no reads of installer-side secret paths (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc), no environment scraping, no obfuscated destinations, and no install-time lifecycle hook that auto-executes these scripts. The rclone install.sh fetches from rclone's official domain, which is aggressive-but-legitimate runtime tool installation rather than a dropper. The scripts fire only when a user explicitly invokes the corresponding skill, not on `npm install`.

Any computer that has this package installed or running should be considered fully compromised. All secrets and keys stored on that computer should be rotated immediately from a different computer. The package should be removed, but as full control of the computer may have been given to an outside entity, there is no guarantee that removing the package will remove all malicious software resulting from installing it.

Out-of-bounds write vulnerability in certain ASUS routers allows an unauthenticated nearby user to corrupt process memory, potentially resulting in a denial-of-service, via crafted LLTD packets.Refer to the ' Security Update for ASUS Router Firmware ' section on the ASUS Security Advisory for more information.

Gogs through 0.14.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated users to view private forks by querying fork listings without per-fork read checks. Attackers with read access to a private base repository can call GET /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/forks or the Forks web handler to obtain other users' private fork owners, names, descriptions and clone URLs.

Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization and Use After Free in certain ASUS router models allows an unauthenticated nearby user to cause the service to write unexpected values or crash the system under specific timing conditions.
Refer to the ' Security Update for ASUS Router Firmware ' section on the ASUS Security Advisory for more information.

OS command injection in the a3cli restricted shell in Lantronix S2220 Series 2 allows an authenticated attacker to bypass shell restrictions and execute arbitrary operating system commands via unsanitized command substitution metacharacters, including backticks and $(), in parameters of permitted commands over SSH. This vulnerability is fixed in firmware version 1.3.37.

A vulnerability was detected in amirhamza05 Student-Management-System up to 449397e35d42e3779f14f0bfc654ab307103f7e3. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file page_action/nav_bar/sql_editor.php of the component SQL Editor. The manipulation of the argument sql_editor_run results in missing authorization. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. This product takes the approach of rolling releases to provide continious delivery. Therefore, version details for affected and updated releases are not available. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

Improper input validation in Variations in Google Chrome prior to 158.0.8127.88 allowed a remote attacker to potentially execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: Critical)

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.7.1 through 0.8.4, an incomplete IPv6 blocklist in AutoGPT's outbound SSRF protection allows authenticated users to reach local or private network services. Specifically, _is_ip_blocked and BLOCKED_IP_NETWORKS in autogpt_platform/backend/backend/util/request.py fail to reject the IPv6 unspecified address :: (which connects to ::1 on Linux) as well as 6to4, NAT64, Teredo, and deprecated IPv4-compatible IPv6 encodings. An attacker can pass :: directly to blocks/sql_query_block.py or blocks/email_block.py, or point URL-fetching blocks, web fetch, MCP servers, webhooks, or OAuth at a hostname whose AAAA record resolves to ::. On backends run directly on a host, this exposes unauthenticated internal RPC services and databases listening on ::1, though the default Docker Compose and single-container deployments bind internal services to IPv4 only. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From 4.5.00 until 4.5.13 and 4.6.02, an unauthenticated attacker can place a multiply encoded value in the news module search q parameter. $nv_Request->get_title() decodes and sanitizes the input once, but modules/news/funcs/search.php subsequently applies urldecode() after sanitization. The resulting raw keyword reaches the {KEY} search-input attribute through search_theme() and the no-results element through search_result_theme() in the default and mobile themes, permitting attribute or tag injection and same-origin JavaScript execution when a victim opens the crafted search URL. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.13 and 4.6.02.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From 4.5.00 until 4.6.01, an authenticated settings-module administrator can upload a PKCS#12 S/MIME certificate whose X.509 Subject CN contains path separators and traversal components. The smimeadd handler in admin/settings/smtp.php applies only an at-sign replacement before using the CN in .key, .crt, and .pem paths beneath data/certs. Traversal can select attacker-chosen paths outside data/certs, but writes remain constrained to already-existing writable directories and the permitted extensions. Within that constraint, attacker-controlled PEM data can overwrite certificate assets, including a DKIM private key; when the curl.cainfo PHP directive is empty, the attacker can also replace cacert.pem and undermine outbound TLS verification. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

The Web-Based Management (WBM) authorization model does not properly enforce permissions for all PROFIBUS configuration operations. A low-privileged remote attacker can abuse an exposed configuration function to modify root-owned PROFIBUS parameters, including device addressing and SSA settings. This allows unauthorized changes to fieldbus-related configuration and violates the intended privilege boundaries within the management interface.

SportEase is a web application for managing school sports events, class rosters, and competition teams. Prior to 1.3, an authenticated account with is_profile_complete=false can submit an attacker-selected class_id for any class in the currently active event to PUT /api/user/profile during first profile completion. AuthHandler.UpdateProfile accepts the class without validating the user's legitimate membership and automatically derives and assigns the corresponding {class_name}_rep role while isFirstCompletion is true. The attacker can become representative of one selected class, view roster information including email addresses, and add or remove competition-team assignments. Downstream handlers correctly reject access to other classes, so the impact is bounded to the selected class, but the representative privilege cannot be revoked through the exposed API and requires direct database intervention or another out-of-band remediation method. This issue is fixed in version 1.3.

Pozeiden is a MermaidJS renderer written in Zig. Prior to 0.3.0, Pozeiden emits attacker-controlled Mermaid values into SVG attributes or markup without sufficient XML escaping or URL scheme validation, and first-party consumers such as zigmark and policypress embed the generated SVG raw into HTML. The click href syntax can introduce a dangerous URL scheme or break out of an attribute; style, classDef, ::: class assignment, and linkStyle color values can inject fill or stroke markup; color and font-weight values can escape text attributes; %%{init}%% themeVariables can inject global renderer attributes; and quadrant y-axis labels can introduce raw markup. These paths involve src/svg/writer.zig, src/renderers/flowchart.zig, src/renderers/quadrant.zig, and src/root.zig. An attacker who can influence rendered Mermaid source can therefore store script-bearing SVG that executes when another user views the published HTML. This issue is fixed in version 0.3.0.
